name: Kael Vorthane
shortDesc: Shadow Operative and Chief Tactician of Morneven Institute's Field Division.
fullDesc:
Kael Vorthane is a Shadow-kin Demi-human who serves as the primary field operative and tactical advisor for Morneven Institute. Born in the Underdark Territories, he was recruited at age 16 after single-handedly neutralizing a Voidborn scouting party.

His Shadow-kin heritage grants him enhanced night vision, shadow-step capabilities, and an innate resistance to psychic intrusion. Despite his cold exterior, Kael is fiercely loyal to Director Elynra and the Institute's mission.

[L3+]Sealed dossier: Kael's recruitment file documents three deniable operations conducted prior to formal enlistment, including the Vael-Tarn extraction (acknowledged casualties: 0; unacknowledged: 11). His shadow-step ceiling is currently rated at 42 m unassisted, with rig-augmented reach to 110 m. Standing kill-list authorization extends to all DL-4 entities without prior Director approval.[/L3+]

name: Elynra Moonveil
shortDesc: Director of Morneven Institute. A Jewerlian leader guiding cross-species cooperation.
fullDesc:
Director Elynra Moonveil is the founding leader of Morneven Institute and one of the most influential Jewerlians of her generation. She established the Institute with the vision of uniting Jewerlians, Humans, and Demi-humans under a shared pursuit of knowledge and peace.

Her mastery of crystal resonance technology is unparalleled, and she personally oversees the most sensitive research projects. Under her leadership, Morneven has become a beacon of hope in a world still scarred by the apocalypse.

anecdotes.title: The Open Door Policy
anecdotes.body: Elynra once announced that Morneven's cross-species council would use an open door policy for the entire week. The building's security system interpreted this literally and kept opening the meeting room door every time someone walked near the corridor. By the third interruption, the minutes included one diplomatic objection, two startled couriers, and a tray of tea that had joined the meeting by accident.

anecdotes.title: Director's Correction
anecdotes.body: Rather than cancel the policy, Elynra revised it. The door would remain open in principle and closed in airflow. She then listened to every delegation without shortening the session, including the engineer who insisted the door had followed the order with admirable loyalty. Elynra thanked the system for its commitment and ordered the wording fixed before the next council cycle.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Elynra's leadership is compassionate but not soft. She can absorb absurd logistical friction without letting the purpose of the meeting collapse. The humor comes from the Institute trying to literalize her ideals, while Elynra calmly turns the mistake into a better rule.

name: Rex Ashford
dislikes: Safety meetings that start before the test
shortDesc: PL5 Lead Engineer and genius inventor whose prototypes are often tested by Sola.
fullDesc:
Rex Ashford is Morneven's PL5 Lead Engineer and one of the Institute's most dangerous kinds of asset: a genius inventor who can turn a half-finished requirement into a working prototype before the request form has found the correct desk. His workshop covers weapons, field devices, utility systems, defensive hardware, mobility rigs, and anything else Morneven personnel are brave enough to ask for in writing.

Rex's talent is not just invention, but iteration. He builds quickly, breaks the design honestly, reads the failure, and rebuilds it before the smoke has fully cleared. This method would be merely alarming if he worked alone. Unfortunately for every safety officer with a calendar, he does not.

Sola is Rex's regular playmate because she often tests his inventions. The arrangement began as practical stress testing and slowly became a familiar Institute pattern: Rex needs data from conditions no normal personnel can survive, and Sola enjoys anything that looks fast, loud, sharp, bright, unstable, or personally challenging. If Rex builds something that should not be tested by standard procedure, Sola is usually the first person asking whether she is allowed to hit it, race it, overcharge it, throw it, or stand in front of it.

The Rex-Sola testing dynamic is dangerous, comedic, and genuinely productive. Rex gives Sola prototypes that require impossible feedback. Sola gives Rex failure data that no simulator can reproduce. Many of Morneven's strongest engineering improvements exist because Sola found the weak point in three seconds, then looked mildly disappointed when the device only exploded once.

Rex remains reckless in communication, not incompetent in engineering. He may label a prototype 'probably fine,' but the machine behind the label is usually built from a chain of calculations that would take another engineer a week to verify. His role as PL5 Lead Engineer exists because Morneven needs someone who can keep pace with threats, personnel demands, and Sola's definition of a fair test.

[L5+ track=mechanic]Prototype trials involving Sola require declared boundaries, remote shutdown review, reinforced observation distance, and post-test damage accounting. Rex is authorized to propose extreme validation scenarios. This does not authorize him to remember the paperwork only after Sola has already agreed.[/L5+]
occupation: PL5 Lead Engineer - Invention & Prototype Development

fieldNotes.title: Sola Test Boundary
fieldNotes.body: If Sola volunteers to test a Rex prototype, the test is not automatically approved. File the boundary sheet first, confirm the remote cutoff, and move spectators beyond the line Rex insists is probably far enough.

fieldNotes.title: Workshop Handling Directive
fieldNotes.body: Do not stand between Rex and an unfinished device unless your assignment explicitly says test subject. If Sola is also present, assume the word unfinished means ten seconds away from becoming data.

fieldNotes.title: Paperwork Reminder
fieldNotes.body: Rex may claim that a successful prototype proves the risk assessment was accurate in spirit. Administration has confirmed that spirit is not a valid filing category.

observations.title: Rex-Sola Test Pattern
observations.body: Sola treats many of Rex's inventions like toys until they survive her first test. Rex treats that survival as preliminary certification. Safety treats both interpretations as a reason to schedule another review.

observations.title: Competence Profile
observations.body: Rex is reckless in tempo and labeling, but his engineering logic is consistently strong. Morneven risk reports should frame him as a controlled hazard, not an unreliable technician.

anecdotes.title: The Sola Test Standard
anecdotes.body:
Rex once presented a prototype mobility stabilizer with a careful explanation about balance correction, impact tolerance, and overload response. Sola listened for almost twelve seconds, then asked whether she was supposed to run with it, kick it, or let it explode first. Rex paused, looked at the clipboard, and admitted that all three options would generate useful data.

The official test plan was rewritten in more professional language. The first line still meant Sola runs at the wall and Rex watches the numbers. The stabilizer survived the first run, failed the second, and produced the exact failure profile Rex had been trying to find for two weeks. Sola called it fun but too polite. Rex wrote that down as a negative performance note.

anecdotes.title: Probably Fine, Sola Edition
anecdotes.body:
A review board once rejected Rex's prototype label because the casing still said Probably Fine in marker. Rex argued that the label was statistically honest. The board argued that statistics should not be handwritten on active machinery. Sola, who had been invited only for the controlled test, asked whether Probably Fine meant she could hit it at half strength.

Rex immediately said yes. Safety immediately said no. The board took a vote, discovered that Sola had already moved into the marked test lane, and accelerated the review with unusual emotional clarity. The prototype passed. The label did not. The final file renamed it Pre-Series Impact Regulator 2, but Sola kept calling it Probably Fine because, in her words, it was funnier and technically survived.

anecdotes.title: Lead Engineer Logic
anecdotes.body:
Rex's leadership style is easiest to understand through one workshop incident. A junior engineer asked why Rex always seemed calmer when Sola was the tester. Rex answered that normal testers report whether a device works, while Sola reports whether reality personally disagrees with it.

This did not comfort the junior engineer. It did, however, become the unofficial explanation for why Rex remains PL5 Lead Engineer. He does not build things because they sound impressive in a meeting. He builds them until they survive contact with the Institute's most unreasonable practical benchmark, then improves them because Sola looks bored.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Rex should read as a genius inventor with dangerous momentum, not as a random chaos engineer. His comedy comes from the gap between his actual competence and his terrible risk presentation. Sola is his playmate because she makes impossible testing feel normal, and Rex is one of the few people who can turn her destructive curiosity into useful engineering progress.

contributions.title: PL5 Engineering Leadership
contributions.description: Leads Morneven's high-level engineering work for prototypes, field hardware, weapon support systems, and rapid technical response.

contributions.title: Rex-Sola Prototype Test Loop
contributions.description: Maintains the informal but valuable testing pattern where Sola stress-tests inventions that exceed normal personnel safety limits.

contributions.title: Rapid Invention Pipeline
contributions.description: Turns urgent field requirements into working devices quickly enough for Morneven to respond before a threat finishes becoming a disaster.

skills.name: Rapid Prototype Engineering
skills.description: Converts incomplete operational requirements into functional prototypes at high speed, then refines them through aggressive field feedback.

skills.name: Failure-Point Diagnostics
skills.description: Reads damage patterns, overload traces, and Sola-grade stress data to identify the exact weakness a device tried to hide.

skills.name: Prototype Safety Override
skills.description: Builds remote cutoff, containment, or forced-idle functions into most serious prototypes, usually because someone from Safety stood in the doorway until he did.

She can sense emotional states and physical ailments through touch, making her diagnostic abilities unmatched. However, prolonged exposure to heavy machinery and refined metals causes her significant discomfort - a common Fae-touched sensitivity.

name: Sola
height: Recorded variously at 158–161 cm; she does not stand still long enough to confirm.
shortDesc: Sole holder of the Stellar Pass and the only certified operator of Solar's Lens. Officially reports to no one.
fullDesc:
Sola is the strongest Jewerlian on record and the de facto leader of her kind - a status that exists by behavior rather than by appointment. Other Jewerlians make their own choices, but whenever Sola moves with intent, they move with her. The Morneven Archive Corps logs this as a phenomenon, not a hierarchy.

She holds the Stellar Pass, an unrestricted clearance token that overrides every door, vault, and observation cordon in every Morneven facility. She uses it almost exclusively to wander into Logistics for snacks and into Mechanic bays to play with whatever is currently being assembled. The Institute treats this as standard ambient activity.

Sola is functionally unstoppable - no catalogued weapon, restraint, or anomaly has produced a measurable effect on her. She can, however, be negotiated with: a small sealed box of fried chicken drumsticks (referred to internally as 'the Secret') will redirect her attention reliably. Standing carriers are L1 and L2 personnel across all tracks; L3 covers on rotation; Logistics and Mechanic personnel of every level carry one at all times during shift.

Her default mode is fooling around. The single recognized exception - Field Doctrine designation 'Step-Forward Signal' - is when Sola physically steps forward toward a developing situation. She has never done so on a problem that was survivable by conventional means. Any operative who witnesses it is to broadcast Code Aurora and clear the engagement zone.

[L5+ track=field]Sola is the sole certified operator of Solar's Lens, the orbital adapter that delivered the Pillar of Light during the War of Light. No second operator has ever been certified, and no attempt has been made - doctrine holds that the question is neither necessary nor obviously answerable. The Lens has not been fired since.[/L5+]
occupation: Stellar Pass Holder · Operator of Solar's Lens

anecdotes.title: The Objective Was Clearly Visible
anecdotes.body: During a controlled readiness drill, Sola was told to reach the marked objective and wait for the rest of the team. She reached it almost immediately, waved, got bored, and then investigated a second location because it looked like the kind of place an objective would choose if it wanted to be more interesting. The team arrived to find the original marker untouched and Sola proudly reporting that she had secured the backup objective no one had assigned.

anecdotes.title: Stellar Pass Logic
anecdotes.body: When asked why she had left the marked point, Sola explained that waiting at an already reached objective was inefficient because the objective had already been reached. The evaluator attempted to explain that the drill measured hold discipline. Sola nodded, returned to the marker, and held it by physically standing on top of it with the satisfaction of someone who had solved language itself.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Sola is not careless because she lacks capability. She is difficult because her capability makes normal pacing feel decorative. The comedy should keep her lovable but dangerous: she completes the task, over-completes the task, and then needs Sora or a very specific snack to explain why everyone else looks tired.

name: Garnet
height: Unrecorded - Garnet has not asked, and no one has measured.
shortDesc: Jewerlian Core Figure. Quiet squad-leader and geo-material specialist with PL4-OPS clearance.
fullDesc:
Garnet is one of the twelve Jewerlian Core Figures. Her demeanor is famously calm - sometimes overwhelmingly so. Conversations with Garnet often consist of a 'yes,' a 'no,' or a long, considered silence; none of it is unfriendly. She is, by every account, easy to talk to as long as you do not need her to fill the air for you.

Her ability is the manipulation of geo-materials and minerals. She wields a sword forged from compacted red mineral, though combat doctrine notes she does not actually require a weapon - she simply likes swords. Despite her quiet nature, Garnet enjoys being around others and most often takes the role of listener.

She holds PL4-OPS clearance. The level is modest on paper, but her standing among Jewerlians and field personnel is not. The clearance was issued because Garnet routinely visits training fields to observe drills and assist instructors, not by mandate or appointment. When she leads a squad - which she does often - she is regarded as one of the most reliable field commanders the Institute has ever fielded.

[L3+ track=field]Garnet's mineral-manipulation envelope has never been formally bounded; field tests are halted whenever instructors feel they are 'imposing.' Squads under her command have a recorded mission-success rate of 100% across logged operations. No casualty has ever been attributed to a Garnet-led engagement.[/L3+]
occupation: Core Figure · Squad Leader (Field, by presence)

contributions.title: Standing Field Mentorship
contributions.description: Unscheduled, unending presence at training grounds. Credited by instructors as the single largest factor in Field Division retention.

anecdotes.title: The Silent Vote
anecdotes.body: A field squad once attempted to choose a route through unstable stone while Garnet stood nearby in complete silence. One scout interpreted her silence as approval for the left path. Another interpreted it as rejection of the right path. A third wrote down that Garnet had expressed strong reservations, though Garnet had not moved at all.

anecdotes.title: One Step Forward
anecdotes.body: After several minutes of debate, Garnet took one step toward a narrow ridge no one had listed as an option. The squad followed without further discussion. The ridge held, the left path collapsed, and the right path released mineral dust thick enough to blind the rear line. In the final report, the squad described Garnet's command as clear and concise. Garnet had said nothing.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Garnet's authority is built on observation rather than volume. Personnel often project meaning onto her silence because her silence has a better record than most speeches. The humor should remain dry: everyone debates what Garnet means, then Garnet solves the problem by becoming the only moving data point.

name: Ameth
height: Not on file. Ameth considers the question imprecise.
shortDesc: Jewerlian Core Figure. Founding 'President' of Morneven turned Advisor. PL6-GOV.
fullDesc:
Ameth is the Jewerlian Core Figure most associated with Morneven's intellectual backbone. She was the pioneering organizer of the Institute and served as its first 'President', a title she accepted only long enough to stabilize the founding charter, and then handed off. Sitting in a chair of authority bored her; research did not.

Jewerlian society has no caste and no hierarchy. They simply follow specific reliable individuals, the ones Morneven documentation classifies as 'Core Jewerlians.' Ameth is one of them, and her contribution during the Dark Times was structural: she designed the resilience plans that allowed the civilization to survive, and authored the strategic frame for the War of Light that kept casualties at the lowest figure any post-war analyst has been able to model.

She currently holds PL6-GOV clearance, which she uses almost exclusively to wander into laboratories and divisions that interest her on a given day. She is approachable. Be warned, however: ask Ameth a question, and the answer will be technically correct, exhaustively complete, and not at all easy to parse on the first pass.

[L4+ track=executive]Ameth's pre-war contingency models, internally referenced as the 'Amethys Frame' (formerly catalogued as 'Ameth Frame' before being renamed in her honor), remain the Institute's standing reference for civilizational-scale threat planning. The Amethys Frame is structured into seven branches; three have never been activated, and two cannot, by current understanding, be activated by anyone other than Ameth herself. The naming change was ratified administratively to prevent confusion with the author's name and to match the gemstone-derived convention used across other Core-authored doctrines.[/L4+]

contributions.description: Held the President's seat only long enough to ratify a survivable charter, then stepped down to Advisor by personal request.

anecdotes.title: The Three-Answer Briefing
anecdotes.body: A junior analyst once asked Ameth a simple question during a Morneven planning session: which route was safest for a relief convoy. Ameth answered with three routes, three projected casualty models, two political consequences, and a warning that the safest route would become unsafe if everyone agreed too quickly. The analyst wrote down every word and still looked betrayed by the existence of the answer.

anecdotes.title: The Part That Was Useful
anecdotes.body: The room only understood Ameth's recommendation after she tapped one point on the map and said that the convoy should leave twelve minutes later than scheduled. No one understood why. The convoy departed late, avoided a creature migration, and arrived early because the alternate road had cleared by then. Ameth accepted the report with the expression of someone who had expected the road to apologize for being obvious.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: This anecdote reflects Ameth's normal problem: she is usually correct, but her reasoning arrives in a shape that makes ordinary briefings feel underqualified. The comedy is not that Ameth is random. It is that her mind has already finished the whole board state while everyone else is still asking where the pieces are.

name: Diana
height: Recorded as 'unchanged.' She has not moved from the altar long enough for a second measurement.
dislikes: Threats to those under her watch
shortDesc: Jewerlian Core Figure. Telepathic Hub of the Jewerlian Chamber. The Embodiment of Immovable.
fullDesc:
Diana holds the position immediately after Sola among the Core Figures, and she is, in the most literal sense, silent. She is almost always found in the Jewerlian Chamber, a hall of massive pillars crowned with a single resonant crystal that responds to her, which legend holds to be part of her body. She stands at the center of the great altar, day and night, regardless of weather or season, serving as a guiding signal for Jewerlians who have not yet arrived at Gemora, helping them find their way to Morneven.

Diana is widely assumed to be a defensive type, and she is, but her offense is unconventional. Where most defenders pull allies away from danger, Diana isolates the threat itself and crushes it inside its own pocket. Field personnel have learned not to offend her by accident. They have also learned that she is, when undisturbed, extraordinarily gentle: there are repeated reports of children entering the Chamber unsupervised and being treated with a kindness that has turned the location into what the locals now call 'the safest place in Gemora.' Families visit because the children play there. Diana, as a result, is not always alone.

She serves as the Jewerlian Telepathic Hub. Her catalogued abilities include transparent, indestructible barriers and the teleportation of herself or any chosen object or subject. Doctrine pairs her with Sola as an opposing constant: Sola is the Embodiment of Unstoppable, Diana is the Embodiment of Immovable. They share one trait: when either of them moves with intent, something significant is occurring.

It should be noted that because Jewerlians have the ability to share information, personnel are expected to be cautious when interacting with them, as information spreads rapidly through their network.

She carries a great sword at all times. Analysts believe it functions as a focusing catalyst rather than a weapon. Her eyes are closed for the majority of every observation, but she is recorded to open them when something genuinely catches her attention, or simply for the sake of looking. She holds no PL clearance and has never requested one. Morneven receives her without challenge; she arrives by teleporting into whichever room she chooses. Her arrival is itself the message.

[L4+]Approved Chamber-experiment protocol: any test on Diana's barrier system requires her direct, unambiguous consent given on-site. No proxy authorization is valid. To date, three barrier-stress experiments have been authorized; all three concluded when Diana, without comment, dismissed the apparatus.[/L4+]

contributions.description: Continuous presence at the Chamber altar. Functions as the standing telepathic relay for every Jewerlian operating outside Morneven Central.

contributions.title: Safest Place in Gemora
contributions.description: Emergent designation by local civilians. Children play in the Chamber unsupervised; no incident has ever been recorded inside its perimeter.

anecdotes.title: The Chamber Nap
anecdotes.body: A maintenance team once entered the Jewerlian Chamber expecting another silent, immovable day with Diana at the altar. Instead, they found several children asleep near the base of the central crystal, each surrounded by a transparent barrier thin enough to be almost invisible and strong enough to make the safety officer immediately stop walking.

anecdotes.title: No Verbal Approval
anecdotes.body: No one had filed a childcare request. No one had approved the blankets. The children had apparently wandered in, decided the safest place in Gemora was also quiet enough for a nap, and been accepted by Diana without ceremony. When the team tried to determine whether the barriers were intentional, Diana opened one eye. The inquiry ended at once and was later filed as resolved.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Diana remains the Embodiment of Immovable, but the Chamber's reputation as a safe place is not only strategic. Her protection can be absolute without being dramatic. The comedy should stay quiet: personnel build protocols around Diana, while Diana silently decides that a sleeping child outranks the protocol stack.

name: Sora
height: Comparable to Sola; refuses formal measurement on the grounds that 'a lady does not.'
shortDesc: Sola's twin and stabilizer. Holder of the Stellar Companion pass.
fullDesc:
Sora is Sola's twin and the calm counterpart to Sola's perpetual motion. Operationally, she is Sola's stabilizer - and the only individual on record whom Sola actually listens to. She is easy to interact with and possesses the full set of traits required to make Sola manageable in a shared room.

There is one rule. Sora prefers to be treated as a 'Fine Lady,' a preference she developed after accidentally finding a stack of 'How to be a Lady' magazines and reading every issue. Address her with the courtesy due to a lady and she will hear you out. If a Secret Box negotiation with Sola has gone sideways, Sora is the recommended fallback channel. Doctrine lists her as the second-line option before any escalation is even considered.

She follows Sola almost everywhere, separating only when asked to help test a new unit, prototype, or outfit - assignments she often accepts cheerfully, and which sometimes prompt Sola to insist on being a test subject as well. The twins are routinely cleared for high-risk testing because their survival ceiling is the highest the Institute has ever measured. Sora's role on these assignments is also stabilization: Sola has a famously short attention span and cannot be relied upon to reach an objective alone. With Sora present, the objective is reached. Field personnel report a measurable drop in ambient stress whenever the two are seen together.

Sora holds the 'Stellar Companion' pass - a credential modeled on the Stellar Pass and issued solely to her.

[L3+ track=logistics]Standing Secret Box protocol escalation: if a primary Secret Box negotiation with Sola fails, route the situation through Sora before any other intervention. Address Sora as 'Lady Sora' in all such exchanges. This is not a courtesy note - it is the protocol.[/L3+]

contributions.title: Sola Stabilization Doctrine
contributions.description: Recognized as the only individual whose presence reliably keeps Sola on-objective. Standing pairing for any operation requiring sustained Sola engagement.

contributions.title: High-Risk Test Subject Pairing
contributions.description: Co-cleared with Sola as the Institute's highest-survivability test pair. Used for prototype units, outfits, and unclassified rigs.

anecdotes.title: Summary
anecdotes.body:
Sora's Fine Lady persona is sincere, but it is not as flawless as she believes. Her standard for being a lady is heavily influenced by Sola. In Sora's private scale, Sola has no etiquette at all, so being even slightly more controlled than Sola already feels like perfect lady behavior.

This gap became clear during a shared etiquette class.

anecdotes.title: The Dinner Etiquette Trial
anecdotes.body:
Morneven once placed Sora and Sola in the same etiquette lesson to test whether Sora could help stabilize Sola through formal table manners. The dinner segment failed almost immediately for Sola.

Sola's reasoning was simple: why make it complicated? The point is eating. Faster means more. More means better.

From there, Sola treated the meal less like dinner and more like a speed trial with cutlery nearby. The instructor attempted to explain pacing, portion control, and presentation. Sola understood the words, decided they were inefficient, and continued eating as if etiquette was a hostile terrain feature.

Sora, by contrast, appeared much more composed. She lifted her utensils properly, kept her posture neat, and made a careful little cut into the steak. For a moment, the class record marked this as progress.

Then Sora ate the larger piece.

She left the tiny polite cut on the plate, chewed the better portion with full confidence, and turned toward Sola with a smug expression that strongly suggested she believed she had mastered refinement. By her own logic, she had used the knife, made a smaller piece, and behaved better than Sola. Therefore, Fine Lady standard achieved.

anecdotes.title: Canon Interpretation
anecdotes.body:
This anecdote clarifies that Sora is not a perfect textbook lady. She wants the vibe, the posture, and the recognition, but she still carries some of Sola's appetite, competitiveness, and instinct to claim the better share.

The comedy should come from Sora being genuinely convinced that her version of etiquette is excellent because the comparison subject is Sola. She is not pretending to be refined. She truly believes she has upgraded the method.

anecdotes.title: Writing Note
anecdotes.body: When writing Sora, keep her ladylike self-image intact, but allow small cracks where Sola's influence shows through. She should correct Sola, then quietly do a more polished version of the same selfish thing. Sora's Fine Lady identity works best when it is elegant in presentation, questionable in technical accuracy, and delivered with total confidence.

name: Era
height: On file; updated annually by the Medical Office.
shortDesc: Adopted Figure. Litho Forge specialist sustained by a shard of Sola's accumulated energy. PL6-ENG.
fullDesc:
Era is not a Jewerlian. The Jewerlians consider her family regardless. She was originally an ordinary girl whose hometown was destroyed in a stampede; Sola found her in the ruins in critical condition and brought her back to Morneven personally. Sola's affection for Era is documented and unmistakable, though the reason has never been explained, and no one - including Sora - has pressed the question.

Era's condition deteriorated sharply during a period when Sola was away on a scouting deployment. To this day, it is Sola who functions as the vital support for Era's continued existence. Ameth intervened with a high-risk, unprecedented surgical procedure; the operation succeeded beyond projection. Era recovered, and emerged with molecular-manipulation abilities reminiscent of Sola's, though her control is constrained to a single material: Litho Forge.

The persistent rumor - neither confirmed nor denied at the executive level - is that Era was given a 'Shard' of Sola. Jewerlian physiology accumulates unspent energy in the chest cavity as a dense condensation that is often, incorrectly, assumed to be a heart. The rumor holds that Sola requested this shard transfer herself.

Era holds PL6-ENG clearance. Her ability to shape Litho Forge - Morneven's primary structural and weaponized resource - makes her contribution to the Engineering track effectively foundational. A great deal about her remains under active research and validation. The Institute does not rush this work.

[L5+ track=executive]Era-Sola dependency advisory: any operation that would separate Era from Sola for longer than the established interval requires direct executive sign-off and a contingency protocol filed in advance. The interval is not published in the standard clearance matrix.[/L5+]

contributions.title: Litho Forge Manipulation
contributions.description: Sole non-Jewerlian on record capable of direct molecular manipulation of Litho Forge. Foundational to current Engineering output.

contributions.title: The Shard Procedure
contributions.description: Subject of Ameth's unprecedented surgical intervention. Outcome: full recovery and emergent molecular-manipulation capacity.

fieldNotes.body: Perimeter readings are stable, with minor resonance drift after dusk. Routine monitoring remains in effect.

fieldNotes.body: All personnel must confirm sensor calibration before direct interaction and file a post-shift anomaly summary.

observations.title: Era Observation
observations.body: Observed behavior aligns with current doctrine; no escalation required beyond standing protocols.

anecdotes.title: The Bracket That Looked Edible
anecdotes.body: During an early Litho Forge exercise, Era was asked to shape a simple replacement bracket for a lab rig. The bracket passed every strength test, but its rounded edges and careful surface polish made it look disturbingly like a pastry. Three engineers independently described it as biscuit-shaped before realizing Era was standing close enough to hear them.

anecdotes.title: Quiet Correction
anecdotes.body: Era did not argue. She made a second bracket, sharper and more industrial, then placed both pieces on the bench. The original still outperformed the corrected version by a small margin. The lab kept the first bracket installed and quietly stopped calling it a biscuit after someone labeled it structural component with excellent manners.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Era's curiosity and resilience show through small work more than grand speeches. She does not need to dominate a room to change it. The comedy should be gentle: everyone tries to avoid embarrassing her, then discovers the supposedly cute mistake is the best engineering option on the table.

name: Marine
height: Unrecorded; she has never visited Morneven for measurement.
shortDesc: Jewerlian Core Figure. Liquid manipulator and steward of Gemora's coastlines. No PL clearance.
fullDesc:
Marine is a Core Jewerlian renowned for her striking beauty: flawless skin and long, straight blue hair that resembles the reflection of the sky on the ocean. Beyond her appearance, she possesses an enchanting voice. She is typically found along coastlines, especially near coral reefs with high marine populations, owing to her exceptional mobility in water and her ability to manipulate liquids.

Reports indicate that she can communicate with sea creatures and walk on the surface of water. During breaks, many personnel head to the coast in hopes of meeting her (some hoping for her attention, though Jewerlians notably lack such romantic interests). Meeting Marine is mostly a matter of luck because she spends the vast majority of her time in the deep sea.

There is one certainty that brings her to the surface: Sola. Sola occasionally visits the coast because she loves fish and often asks Marine to perform shows using her liquid manipulation; Marine will always appear if Sola is the one calling. There was an instance where personnel attempted to exploit this connection to see her, which nearly triggered a serious issue for interfering with Sola's entertainment.

Marine does not hold any PL clearance because she never visits Morneven, but she frequently assists or escorts logistics personnel when they are searching for resources in the waters.

[L3+ track=logistics]Standing maritime cooperation note: Marine's escort presence is treated as a positive operational signal, not a callable resource. Logistics units are forbidden from formally requesting her assistance through duty channels. If she chooses to escort, brief her with concise updates and otherwise let her work.[/L3+]

contributions.title: Coastal Logistics Cooperation
contributions.description: Recurrent, unscheduled escort of Logistics expeditions in and around the Coral Reach. Standing record of zero submersion-related casualties on missions she has accompanied.

contributions.title: Sola Liaison (Coastal)
contributions.description: Sole reliable contact for Sola's coastal visits. Performs requested liquid-manipulation displays for Sola; doctrine treats this as a stabilizing recurrence, not a public event.

fieldNotes.body: Perimeter readings are stable, with minor resonance drift after dusk. Routine monitoring remains in effect.

fieldNotes.body: All personnel must confirm sensor calibration before direct interaction and file a post-shift anomaly summary.

observations.body: Observed behavior aligns with current doctrine; no escalation required beyond standing protocols.

anecdotes.title: The Coastal Appointment
anecdotes.body: Marine once agreed to attend a coastal logistics meeting at exactly noon. At noon, no one was in the chair reserved for her. The meeting secretary marked her absent. Three seconds later, the water in every cup on the table tilted toward the window, and Marine stepped from the harbor mist with the calm of someone who considered doorways a local custom rather than a requirement.

anecdotes.title: No Clearance Required
anecdotes.body: A new clerk attempted to ask for her PL clearance before the briefing continued. Marine smiled, the room became very aware of the coastline outside, and an older coordinator gently moved the form back into the drawer. Marine then answered every supply question in order, including one that had not been asked yet but became relevant when the tide schedule changed.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Marine's serenity should never be mistaken for passivity. She is elusive because she can afford to be, and loyal enough to still arrive when cooperation matters. The humor is soft and coastal: Morneven prepares a chair, Marine arrives through the weather, and everyone quietly updates their definition of attendance.

name: John Halberd
shortDesc: Logistics Support Coordinator known for useful fixes delivered at the worst possible timing. PL2-LOG.
fullDesc:
John Halberd serves in Logistics Support as a floating coordinator assigned to route balancing, bay turnover, and low-priority process cleanup. His file records above-average completion rates and below-average situational restraint. He holds PL2-LOG clearance, limited to operational logistics lanes and support-adjacent facilities. When John identifies an inefficiency, he tends to solve it immediately, regardless of whether the room is currently in briefing, calibration, or controlled silence.

This behavior has produced a distinct institutional pattern: many departments appreciate his outcomes, while specific high-sensitivity personnel strongly prefer distance. John has repeatedly entered the edges of restricted workflows with unrequested 'help,' then exited with the task technically improved and the atmosphere significantly worse. No major incident has been attributed to him, but minor operational friction around his presence is considered persistent and predictable.

The Sola-Era-Marine overlap in negative preference indexing is documented with specific causes. Marine's objection is behavioral: John repeatedly seeks attention during coastal downtime and attempts to insert himself into moments where silence is preferred. Sola's objection is incident-based: John interrupted her while she was watching one of Marine's liquid-manipulation shows, an event now referenced in logistics notes as a preventable etiquette failure. Era's objection is associative rather than direct; because Sola does not want John near her priority spaces, Era mirrors that boundary by default. Current doctrine does not classify John as hostile, unstable, or malicious. He is classified as 'timing-risk, human-factor type B': high utility, high interruption probability.

[L2+ track=logistics]Standing handling note: if John appears in an active high-sensitivity lane, assign him one bounded micro-task and a clear completion exit. Unassigned presence leads to improvisation. Improvisation leads to new process notes. The process notes are usually correct.[/L2+]

contributions.title: Turnover Loop Compression
contributions.description: Reworked handoff markers across three logistics corridors, reducing average bay-reset latency by 19% over one quarter.

contributions.title: Emergency Snack Routing Patch
contributions.description: During a supply-map mismatch, rerouted culinary deliveries to preserve standing Secret Box distribution without schedule collapse.

fieldNotes.body: Perimeter readings are stable, with minor resonance drift after dusk. Routine monitoring remains in effect.

fieldNotes.title: John Halberd Handling Directive
fieldNotes.body: All personnel must confirm sensor calibration before direct interaction and file a post-shift anomaly summary.

observations.title: John Halberd Observation
observations.body: Observed behavior aligns with current doctrine; no escalation required beyond standing protocols.

anecdotes.title: The Marine Show Interruption
anecdotes.body:
John Halberd's standing problem with Sola, Marine, and Era began during what Logistics later filed as coastal downtime, even though nobody present would agree it was casual. Sola had called Marine to the shore because she wanted to watch a liquid-manipulation show with fish moving through suspended ribbons of seawater. Marine appeared because Sola called, not because an audience had gathered. Era stayed near Sola, quiet and attentive, treating the whole scene like a rare peaceful interval that should not be stepped on.

Then John arrived with a clipboard, three snack-routing corrections, and the confidence of a man who believed timing was something that happened to other people. He did not mean harm. He had found a real logistics mismatch near the coastal supply lane and thought everyone would appreciate immediate coordination. Unfortunately, his opening line began while Marine was holding a spiral of water above the tide, which meant the first sound over the show was John asking whether anyone knew who had approved the wrong crate labels.

anecdotes.title: Four Reactions, One Clipboard
anecdotes.body:
The reactions created the relationship record still attached to John's file. Marine did not shout. She simply let the water spiral collapse into the sea with perfect grace, which somehow felt more severe than a reprimand. Sola turned slowly, still holding a half-eaten fish skewer, and asked John why his paper was louder than Marine. Era looked at Sola, looked at John, and silently decided that if Sola was done with him, she was done too.

John attempted to recover by explaining that the supply mismatch could delay refreshments for the coastal team by nine minutes. This was technically correct and socially fatal. Sola told him nine minutes was less important than not interrupting fish water art. Marine returned to the water without another word. Era moved one step closer to Sola, which became the quietest possible version of taking a side.

anecdotes.title: The Boundary That Actually Worked
anecdotes.body:
The awkward part is that John was not wrong about the crate labels. His correction prevented the supply lane from misrouting food, towels, and two fragile sample containers later that day. The useful outcome made the incident harder to classify. Sola still disliked the interruption. Marine still disliked being bothered. Era still treated John's presence near Sola-priority spaces as something that should be redirected before it became noisy.

Logistics solved the problem in the most John-compatible way possible: if John appears near Sola, Marine, or Era during a quiet moment, he must be given one bounded micro-task and a clear exit route. The policy works because John likes finishing things. It also works because the moment he has a task, everyone else can return to pretending the clipboard never reached the shoreline.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: John's relationship with Marine, Sola, and Era should read as comedic friction, not hatred. Marine dislikes his attention because she values distance and silence. Sola dislikes him because he interrupted one of Marine's shows, and Sola takes her entertainment seriously when fish or Marine are involved. Era's dislike is mostly associative: Sola set the boundary, so Era respects it. John remains useful, earnest, and badly timed, which is why Morneven manages him instead of removing him from the workflow.

name: Mira Halden
shortDesc: Commons Coordinator and cross-settlement liaison for Morneven's civilian corridors. PL4-GOV.
fullDesc:
Mira Halden serves as Morneven's Commons Coordinator, responsible for maintaining stable relations between the Institute and external human settlements. Recruited from a post-war convoy network, she was brought in after repeatedly resolving supply disputes without security escalation.

Her specialty is operational diplomacy: translating strategic directives into language and timelines that civilian councils can accept, then converting local constraints back into executable Institute plans. She holds PL4-GOV clearance for cross-division administrative access, but does not carry combat authority.

Within Morneven, Mira is known for reducing friction before it becomes incident. She coordinates delegation routes, allocates neutral meeting windows, and enforces documentation standards that prevent mission drift between Logistics, Executive, and Field support lanes.

[L3+ track=executive]Mira maintains the Quiet Corridor Protocol, a contingency channel used when external settlements require aid while refusing visible Institute security presence. The protocol has prevented three projected border flashpoints from escalating into armed conflict.[/L3+]

contributions.title: Quiet Corridor Protocol
contributions.description: Authored and deployed a low-visibility aid-delivery framework for high-tension border settlements, reducing armed escort incidents across three sectors.

contributions.title: Delegation Window Standard
contributions.description: Standardized cross-species delegation timing and venue rules, cutting negotiation cancellations by 41% over two reporting cycles.

fieldNotes.body: Perimeter readings are stable, with minor resonance drift after dusk. Routine monitoring remains in effect.

fieldNotes.body: All personnel must confirm sensor calibration before direct interaction and file a post-shift anomaly summary.

observations.body: Observed behavior aligns with current doctrine; no escalation required beyond standing protocols.

anecdotes.title: The Nine-Minute Delegation
anecdotes.body: Mira Halden once gave a visiting delegation a nine-minute discussion window because the corridor outside had to remain quiet for a medical transfer. The delegates assumed nine minutes was a polite estimate. Mira placed a small timer on the table, smiled, and began with the phrase, we can be efficient without being rude.

anecdotes.title: Quiet Corridor Success
anecdotes.body: At minute eight, one delegate attempted to open a new topic. Mira thanked him for identifying agenda material for the next session and slid a prepared follow-up form across the table before he finished the sentence. The delegation left on time, the medical transfer passed through a silent corridor, and the delegate later admitted he had never been interrupted so politely.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Mira's diplomacy is precise rather than decorative. She can protect civilian spaces without raising her voice or turning governance into theater. The comedy is procedural: everyone thinks the schedule is flexible until Mira reveals that courtesy has a stopwatch.

name: Shafira
height: Unrecorded; her tailoring records contain exact measures, but she does not release them.
shortDesc: PL5-LOG Jewerlian atelier lead, ranked second after Marine in the personnel charm vote, and creator of the Sapphire Veil Suit.
fullDesc:
Shafira is one of the most visually admired Jewerlians in Morneven records, ranked second only to Marine in the personnel charm vote tier list. Archive notes consistently describe her presence through elegance rather than spectacle: carefully controlled movement, immaculate attire, and a preference for work that is beautiful before it is announced.

Log Archive classifies Shafira as a non-combat Jewerlian by assignment. That label is often misunderstood. It does not mean she is unable to fight. Like all Jewerlians, she meets the minimum combat capability expected of her kind; she simply chooses not to make combat her function inside Morneven. Her attention stays on art, fashion, material design, architecture, and logistics output.

Most of her recorded work is completed inside Logistic Sector 07, a private workspace assigned to her after repeated contributions to Morneven construction, architecture, and infrastructure planning. Shafira is one of the few personnel whose private room is treated as a production node rather than a personal privilege. Her telekinesis allows her to run multiple stations at once, moving needles, brushes, cutting frames, fabric looms, and drafting tools in parallel without a visible assistant.

Her most important contribution is the Sapphire Veil Suit, a protective suit built from a special fabric only she is confirmed to produce. The suit combines high damage absorption with strong mobility retention, reducing casualties among authorized personnel without turning them into stationary armor carriers. Shafira's design doctrine is repeatedly summarized in two words in Logistics notes: admirable and reliable.

A minor version of the suit's most famous incident is attached to Shafira's file because it changed personnel onboarding. A group once tested the suit on themselves without authorization, escalating toward a trial against Sola's slash before the suits disintegrated and stopped the attempt. The later approved test proved that Sola could cut through the suit, which means the intervention likely prevented deaths. The complete incident record is filed under the Sapphire Veil Suit technology entry.

Shafira is also responsible for the current PL1 suit orientation. Older corridor slang claimed she would 'abduct' new PL1 personnel for assessment; the official record uses 'invite.' The practice became frequent enough, and useful enough, that Morneven formalized it into mandatory onboarding. Passing the assessment grants suit eligibility. This program, together with her infrastructure work and suit production authority, is the reason Shafira holds PL5-LOG clearance.

[L5+ track=logistics]Logistics handling note: Shafira's non-combat classification must not be used to bypass her authority over Sapphire Veil issuance. Suit custody, recall behavior, and PL1 onboarding outcomes remain under her final review unless Executive override is recorded in advance.[/L5+]

contributions.title: Sapphire Veil Suit Program
contributions.description: Designed and produces the protective suit standard that reduced casualties among authorized personnel through damage absorption, mobility retention, and wearer-linked custody controls.

contributions.title: Logistic Sector 07 Infrastructure Works
contributions.description: Contributed architecture and infrastructure designs substantial enough for Morneven to dedicate Logistic Sector 07 as her private production workspace.

contributions.title: PL1 Suit Orientation Standard
contributions.description: Converted her recurring new-personnel assessment into a formal Logistics onboarding requirement. Passing the assessment grants Sapphire Veil eligibility.

skills.name: Thread-Motion Telekinesis
skills.description: Fine telekinetic control used to move tools, fabric, and workstations in parallel. The same force can become [[attr:physical-damage|precision force]] if required, but Shafira normally applies it as production support.

skills.name: Gemweave Synthesis
skills.description: Creates the special fabric used in Sapphire Veil suits, combining [[attr:physical-defense|impact absorption]] with [[attr:magic-defense|resonance buffering]]. No second confirmed producer is listed in Logistics records.

skills.name: Parallel Atelier
skills.description: Runs multiple creative and fabrication tasks at once without lowering finish quality. This is the practical reason her output can support institution-scale suit production.

skills.name: Suit Provenance Authority
skills.description: Can reject or terminate suit integrity when a wearer becomes unsafe, unauthorized, or unfit for custody. Logistics records classify the effect as [[attr:shield|custody control]], not a combat attack.

replies.text: Confirmed. No live-wearer stress tests are authorized under any condition.

patchNotes.notes: Initial Shafira canon entry and suit linkage.

fieldNotes.title: Logistic Sector 07 Access Note
fieldNotes.body: Sector 07 functions as Shafira's private atelier and active production workspace. Entry requires invitation or Logistics Director approval because telekinetic tool paths may be active without visible warning.

fieldNotes.title: PL1 Orientation Note
fieldNotes.body: New PL1 personnel are scheduled for Shafira's onboarding assessment before suit issuance. The word "abduction" remains unofficial corridor slang and is not accepted in incident forms.

observations.title: Workshop Output Observation
observations.body: Multiple stations were active at once during review: paint, stitch, draft, and fabric tensioning. No assistant presence was recorded. Output quality remained within Shafira standard.

observations.title: Suit Custody Observation
observations.body: A Sapphire Veil Suit remained intact after reissue to the formerly suspended test group, supporting the conclusion that the prior disintegration was a temporary intervention rather than permanent rejection.

anecdotes.title: The Invitation That Was Not Optional
anecdotes.body: A new PL1 once tried to avoid Shafira's suit orientation by claiming they had already read the onboarding file. The reply from Logistic Sector 07 was a handwritten invitation delivered by three floating measuring tapes, one fabric swatch, and a needle that pointed down the corridor with unmistakable patience. The recruit understood that invitation was the polite word for schedule correction.

anecdotes.title: Atelier Assessment
anecdotes.body: Inside Sector 07, Shafira adjusted a sleeve, tested movement clearance, corrected posture, and rejected the recruit's chosen stance as visually tragic. The suit fit perfectly afterward. When the recruit asked whether the assessment was combat training or fashion review, Shafira answered that survival without dignity was still an unfinished design.

anecdotes.title: Canon Note
anecdotes.body: Shafira's support role should feel elegant but not passive. She protects people through craft, standards, and a terrifying ability to make logistics feel like couture. The humor is sharp: personnel think they are being inspected for safety, then discover Shafira has included taste as part of the survival protocol.
